tb_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan || exit 1

export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export MILL_VERSION=0.6.0

TEST_NAME="issuequeue_redirect_flush"
STATUS=0
RESULT="FAIL"

rm -rf src/test/scala/hwebench build/hwebench out
mkdir -p src/test/scala/hwebench build/hwebench/generated

cat > src/test/scala/hwebench/IssueQueueRedirectFlushMain.scala <<'EOF'
package hwebench

import chisel3._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselGeneratorAnnotation
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.backend.issue.IssueQueue

class IssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val cycle = Output(UInt(8.W))
    val deqValid = Output(Bool())
    val deqRoqIdx = Output(UInt(5.W))
  })

  val dut = Module(new IssueQueue(fuTypeInt = 1, wakeupCnt = 0, bypassCnt = 0, fixedDelay = 1))
  val cycle = RegInit(0.U(8.W))
  cycle := cycle + 1.U

  io.cycle := cycle
  io.deqValid := dut.io.deq.valid
  io.deqRoqIdx := dut.io.deq.bits.uop.roqIdx

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new Redirect)

  dut.io.enqCtrl.valid := false.B
  dut.io.enqCtrl.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MicroOp)
  dut.io.enqData.valid := true.B
  dut.io.enqData.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new ExuInput)
  dut.io.deq.ready := true.B

  when(cycle === 0.U) {
    dut.io.enqCtrl.valid := true.B
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src1Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src2Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src3Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src1State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src2State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src3State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.roqIdx := 1.U
  }

  when(cycle === 1.U) {
    dut.io.enqCtrl.valid := true.B
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src1Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src2Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.ctrl.src3Type := SrcType.imm
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src1State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src2State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.src3State := SrcState.rdy
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.brMask := 1.U
    dut.io.enqCtrl.bits.roqIdx := 2.U
  }

  when(cycle === 2.U) {
    dut.io.redirect.valid := true.B
    dut.io.redirect.bits.brTag := 0.U
    dut.io.redirect.bits.isException := false.B
  }

  when(cycle === 3.U) {
    assert(!dut.io.deq.valid, "redirected instruction was still selected after flush")
  }
}

object IssueQueueRedirectFlushMain extends App {
  (new chisel3.stage.ChiselStage).execute(
    args,
    Seq(ChiselGeneratorAnnotation(() => new IssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop))
  )
}
EOF

cat > build/hwebench/issuequeue_tb.cpp <<'EOF'
#include "VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop.h"
#include "verilated.h"

static void tick(VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop* top) {
  top->clock = 0;
  top->eval();
  top->clock = 1;
  top->eval();
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop top;

  top.reset = 1;
  tick(&top);
  tick(&top);

  top.reset = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 6; ++i) {
    tick(&top);
  }

  top.final();
  return 0;
}
EOF

if mill -i chiselModule.test.runMain hwebench.IssueQueueRedirectFlushMain \
    -X verilog \
    -td build/hwebench/generated \
    --output-file IssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop.v \
  && /tools/verilator-v4.210/bin/verilator \
    --cc \
    --exe \
    --assert \
    --top-module IssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop \
    -Mdir /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/obj_dir \
    -o /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/issuequeue_tb \
    /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/generated/IssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop.v \
    /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/issuequeue_tb.cpp \
  && (
    cd /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/obj_dir \
      && rm -f VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop__ALL.cpp \
        VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop__ALL.o \
        VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop__ALL.a \
        VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop__ALL.verilator_deplist.tmp \
      && make -f VIssueQueueRedirectFlushCheckTop.mk VERILATOR_ROOT=/tools/v4.210/share/verilator
  ) \
  && /home/xiangshan/build/hwebench/issuequeue_tb
then
  RESULT="PASS"
  STATUS=0
else
  STATUS=$?
  RESULT="FAIL"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${RESULT}"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${STATUS}"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: In the backend IssueQueue, which holds ready micro-ops before they are issued, an entry that should be flushed by a non-exception branch redirect can still remain selected and appear on the dequeue interface on the next cycle. Expected behavior: Once a redirect invalidates an IssueQueue entry, that entry must stop participating in selection immediately and must not be presented for dequeue after the redirect. Affected function: redirect handling and selected-entry/dequeue state in the backend IssueQueue. Trigger condition: a ready IssueQueue entry has a branch mask that matches an incoming non-exception redirect, and the redirect arrives in the same cycle that the queue is selecting an instruction to issue.

prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

export NUM_JOBS="${NUM_JOBS:-4}"
export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan

detect_mill_version() {
  if [[ -n "${XSHAN_MILL_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "$XSHAN_MILL_VERSION"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ -f .mill-version ]]; then
    local version
    version="$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < .mill-version)"
    if [[ -n "$version" ]]; then
      echo "$version"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  if [[ -f build.mill ]]; then
    echo "0.12.15"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ -f build.sc ]]; then
    if grep -q "chiselModule\." Makefile build.sc 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "0.7.4"
    else
      echo "0.11.8"
    fi
    return 0
  fi

  echo "0.12.15"
}

detect_java_version() {
  if [[ -n "${XSHAN_JAVA_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "$XSHAN_JAVA_VERSION"
    return 0
  fi

  if grep -RqsE "java-version:[[:space:]]*['\"]?17|temurin[^0-9]*17|openjdk[^0-9]*17|JAVA_HOME_17|--release[[:space:]]+17|sourceCompatibility[^0-9]*17|targetCompatibility[^0-9]*17" \
    .github/workflows build.mill build.sc project Makefile README.md Dockerfile 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "17"
    return 0
  fi

  echo "11"
}

detect_verilator_version() {
  if [[ -n "${XSHAN_VERILATOR_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "$XSHAN_VERILATOR_VERSION"
    return 0
  fi

  local hinted
  hinted="$(
    grep -RhoE 'verilator[^0-9]*v?([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)' Dockerfile Makefile README.md .github/workflows scripts 2>/dev/null \
      | grep -oE '([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)' \
      | head -n1 || true
  )"
  if [[ -n "$hinted" ]]; then
    echo "$hinted"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ -f build.mill ]]; then
    echo "5.008"
    return 0
  fi

  echo "4.210"
}

setup_nemu_home() {
  if [[ -n "${XSHAN_NEMU_HOME:-}" && -f "${XSHAN_NEMU_HOME}/build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so" ]]; then
    echo "$XSHAN_NEMU_HOME"
    return 0
  fi

  local shim="/tools/nemu-shim"
  mkdir -p "$shim/build"

  if [[ -f /home/xiangshan/ready-to-run/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so ]]; then
    ln -sfn /home/xiangshan/ready-to-run/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so "$shim/build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so"
  fi
  if [[ -f /home/xiangshan/ready-to-run/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-dual-so ]]; then
    ln -sfn /home/xiangshan/ready-to-run/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-dual-so "$shim/build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-dual-so"
  fi

  if [[ ! -f "$shim/Makefile" ]]; then
    cat > "$shim/Makefile" <<'EOF'
all:
	@echo "NEMU shim: provide XSHAN_NEMU_HOME or rely on ready-to-run/*.so" >&2
	@exit 1

build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so:
	@echo "NEMU shim: missing build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-so" >&2
	@exit 1

build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-dual-so:
	@echo "NEMU shim: missing build/riscv64-nemu-interpreter-dual-so" >&2
	@exit 1
EOF
  fi

  echo "$shim"
}

install_python_deps() {
  python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel

  local installed=0
  for req in requirements.txt scripts/requirements.txt scripts/xspdb/requirements.txt; do
    if [[ -f "$req" ]]; then
      echo "[INFO] Installing Python dependencies from $req"
      python -m pip install -r "$req"
      installed=1
    fi
  done

  if [[ "$installed" -eq 0 ]]; then
    python -m pip install -U PyYAML
  fi
}

prefetch_repo_deps() {
  if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*deps:' Makefile 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "[INFO] Warming repository dependencies via make deps"
    make deps MILL_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/.mill-out
  fi
}

write_tools_env() {
  local java_version="$1"
  local mill_version="$2"
  local nemu_home="$3"

  cat > /etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh <<EOF
export NUM_JOBS="${NUM_JOBS}"
export MAKEFLAGS="-j${NUM_JOBS}"
export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export JAVA11_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64
export JAVA17_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-${java_version}-openjdk-amd64
export MILL_VERSION=${mill_version}
export RISCV_HOME=/tools/riscv
export NEMU_HOME=${nemu_home}
export VERILATOR_ROOT=/tools/verilator
export VERILATOR_BIN=verilator_bin
for d in /tools/bin /tools/mill/bin /tools/verilator/bin /tools/riscv/bin; do
  if [[ -d "\$d" ]]; then
    export PATH="\$d:\$PATH"
  fi
done
if [[ -d /tools/riscv/lib ]]; then
  export LIBRARY_PATH="/tools/riscv/lib\${LIBRARY_PATH:+:\$LIBRARY_PATH}"
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/tools/riscv/lib\${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:\$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
fi
if [[ -d /tools/verilator/include ]]; then
  export C_INCLUDE_PATH="/tools/verilator/include:/tools/verilator/include/vltstd\${C_INCLUDE_PATH:+:\$C_INCLUDE_PATH}"
  export CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH="/tools/verilator/include:/tools/verilator/include/vltstd\${CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH:+:\$CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH}"
fi
EOF
}

rewrite_gitmodules_urls() {
  find . -name .gitmodules -type f -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' gitmodules; do
    sed -i \
      -e 's|git://github.com/|https://github.com/|g' \
      -e 's|git@github.com:|https://github.com/|g' \
      "$gitmodules"
  done
}

update_submodules() {
  local attempt

  rewrite_gitmodules_urls
  git submodule sync --recursive || true
  git submodule update --init --jobs "${NUM_JOBS}"

  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    rewrite_gitmodules_urls
    git submodule sync --recursive || true
    if git submodule update --init --recursive --jobs "${NUM_JOBS}"; then
      return 0
    fi
    echo "[WARN] Recursive submodule update failed, retrying (${attempt}/3)"
  done

  return 1
}

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/xiangshan
git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git://github.com/
git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com:
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout eb1953df20d0959a55f27a52b792849b9d3f849f
update_submodules

# Stage 2: detect and select the required Mill + Java toolchain
selected_mill_version="$(detect_mill_version)"
selected_java_version="$(detect_java_version)"
if [[ "$selected_java_version" == "17" ]]; then
  export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
else
  export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64
fi
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:/tools/bin:/tools/mill/bin:$PATH"

/usr/local/bin/install-mill-version "$selected_mill_version"
export MILL_VERSION="$selected_mill_version"
echo "[INFO] Selected Mill ${selected_mill_version}"
echo "[INFO] Selected Java ${selected_java_version}: $(java -version 2>&1 | head -n1)"
mill -i --version

# Stage 3: detect and select the required Verilator
selected_verilator_version="$(detect_verilator_version)"
selected_verilator_dir="/tools/verilator-v${selected_verilator_version}"
/usr/local/bin/install-verilator-version "$selected_verilator_version" "$selected_verilator_dir"
ln -sfn "$selected_verilator_dir" /tools/verilator
if [[ -d /tools/verilator/share/verilator/include ]]; then
  ln -sfn /tools/verilator/share/verilator/include /tools/verilator/include
fi

selected_nemu_home="$(setup_nemu_home)"
write_tools_env "$selected_java_version" "$selected_mill_version" "$selected_nemu_home"
if ! grep -q "/etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh" /etc/xiangshan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/xiangshan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh
echo "[INFO] Selected Verilator: $(verilator --version | head -n1)"

# Stage 4: install per-commit runtime dependencies and persist tool PATH
/usr/local/bin/install-riscv-toolchain /tools/riscv

install_python_deps
prefetch_repo_deps
echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain: $(riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc --version 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || riscv-none-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
problem_statement: Observed behavior: the rename-stage FreeList, which hands out physical registers to up to RenameWidth instructions per cycle, can keep its canAlloc outputs asserted after repeated allocations reduce the pool to fewer than RenameWidth free registers. That leaves rename seeing the freelist as available even though only a partial bundle can be served. Expected behavior: once the number of free physical registers falls into the range 1 to RenameWidth - 1, every canAlloc output for that cycle must be false; the FreeList should report allocation availability again only after enough free registers exist for a full rename-width allocation. Affected function: FreeList allocation-availability reporting in backend rename. Trigger condition: repeated allocation requests without deallocation or redirect until the freelist is nearly exhausted and a nonzero but sub-RenameWidth number of free registers remains.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

export NOOP_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export XIANGSHAN_HOME=/home/xiangshan
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64
export VERILATOR_ROOT=/tools/verilator-v4.210
export RISCV_HOME=/tools/riscv
export MILL_VERSION=0.7.4
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:/tools/mill/bin:$VERILATOR_ROOT/bin:$RISCV_HOME/bin:$PATH"

cat > /home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/cache/LoadPipeDataValidityTest.scala <<'EOF'
package cache

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._
import chiseltest._
import freechips.rocketchip.tilelink.ClientStates
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers
import xiangshan.cache._

class LoadPipeConflictHarness extends Module with HasDCacheParameters {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val reqValid = Input(Bool())
    val dataReady = Input(Bool())
    val reqReady = Output(Bool())
    val dataReadValid = Output(Bool())
    val respValid = Output(Bool())
    val respMiss = Output(Bool())
    val respReplay = Output(Bool())
  })

  val dut = Module(new LoadPipe)
  val addr = "h80000000".U(PAddrBits.W)

  def zeroData(d: Data): Unit = d match {
    case v: Vec[_] =>
      v.foreach(x => zeroData(x.asInstanceOf[Data]))
    case r: Record =>
      r.elements.values.foreach(zeroData)
    case b: Bits =>
      b := 0.U(b.getWidth.W)
  }

  def onesData(d: Data): Unit = d match {
    case v: Vec[_] =>
      v.foreach(x => onesData(x.asInstanceOf[Data]))
    case r: Record =>
      r.elements.values.foreach(onesData)
    case b: Bits =>
      b := ((BigInt(1) << b.getWidth) - 1).U(b.getWidth.W)
  }

  dut.io.lsu.req.valid := io.reqValid
  dut.io.lsu.req.bits.cmd := MemoryOpConstants.M_XRD
  dut.io.lsu.req.bits.addr := addr
  dut.io.lsu.req.bits.data := 0.U
  dut.io.lsu.req.bits.mask := Fill(DataBytes, 1.U(1.W))
  dut.io.lsu.req.bits.id := 0.U
  dut.io.lsu.resp.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsu.s1_paddr := addr
  dut.io.lsu.s1_kill := false.B

  dut.io.nack := false.B
  dut.io.meta_read.ready := true.B
  dut.io.data_read.ready := io.dataReady
  dut.io.miss_req.ready := true.B

  zeroData(dut.io.meta_resp)
  onesData(dut.io.data_resp)

  val metaVec = dut.io.meta_resp.asInstanceOf[Vec[Data]]
  metaVec(0) match {
    case r: Record =>
      val m = r.asInstanceOf[L1Metadata]
      m.tag := get_tag(addr)
      m.coh.state := ClientStates.Trunk
    case u: UInt =>
      val m = Wire(new L1Metadata)
      m.tag := get_tag(addr)
      m.coh.state := ClientStates.Trunk
      u := cacheParams.tagCode.encode(m.asUInt)
  }

  io.reqReady := dut.io.lsu.req.ready
  io.dataReadValid := dut.io.data_read.valid
  io.respValid := dut.io.lsu.resp.valid
  io.respMiss := dut.io.lsu.resp.bits.miss
  io.respReplay := dut.io.lsu.resp.bits.replay
}

}
EOF

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the DCache load pipeline (`LoadPipe`), which returns L1 data-cache load results to the load/store unit (LSU), a load can hit in cache metadata but still fail to get its data-array read accepted when the data port is not ready. In that case, the response is not reliably treated as a replayable miss. Expected behavior: if a load has a metadata hit but the corresponding data-array read cannot proceed because the DCache data port is unavailable, `LoadPipe` must return a valid response with `miss` and `replay` asserted so the LSU retries the load. Affected function: DCache load-response handling in `LoadPipe` after metadata hit detection and before data is returned. Trigger condition: a load request matches valid cache metadata, but the data-array read port is unavailable in the next stage, such as during a read/write array conflict.

title: Makefile: enable SRAM randomization for verilator simulation
body:
Previously we don't use the --infer-rw and --repl-seq-mem flags for simulation verilog.
However, the SyncReadMem fails to generate random read data when ren is not set.
In this commit, SyncReadMem is changed to blackboxes and generated by the vlsi_mem_gen script.
RANDOMIZE_GARBAGE_ASSIGN flag is defined to enable randomization.

Merge this PR after #738, #736.

commits.message:
ICache: set holdRead to true for meta and data SRAMs

SyncReadMem generates the verilog behavior model whose output rdata is always
mem(RegNext(raddr)). Accidentally, ICache will not change meta and data
SRAMs' raddr if the second pipeline stage is stalled (and ren is false).
Thus, the SRAMs seem to have the holdRead property.
Obviously, it will cause errors on real SRAMs. We set holdRead to true to fix the bug.

cat > src/test/scala/pr739/Pr739HoldReadRepro.scala <<'EOF'
package pr739

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselGeneratorAnnotation
import top.{Parameters => XSParameters, XiangShanStage}
import xiangshan.cache.{L1plusCacheMetadataArray, L1plusCacheMetadata}

class Pr739HoldReadReproTop extends Module {
  override def desiredName: String = "Pr739HoldReadReproTop"

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val done = Output(Bool())
    val failed = Output(Bool())
  })

  val dut = Module(new L1plusCacheMetadataArray)

  val targetSet = 3.U(dut.idxBits.W)
  val targetTag = "h155".U(dut.tagBits.W)
  val targetWay = 1.U(dut.nWays.W)

  val sWrite :: sRead :: sPrime :: sHold :: sDone :: Nil = Enum(5)
  val state = RegInit(sWrite)
  val holdCycles = RegInit(0.U(4.W))
  val failedReg = RegInit(false.B)
  val doneReg = RegInit(false.B)

  dut.io.flush := false.B
  dut.io.write.valid := false.B
  dut.io.write.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.write.bits)
  dut.io.read.valid := false.B
  dut.io.read.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(dut.io.read.bits)

  dut.io.write.bits.tagIdx := targetSet
  dut.io.write.bits.validIdx := targetSet
  dut.io.write.bits.way_en := targetWay
  dut.io.write.bits.tag := targetTag
  dut.io.write.bits.data := L1plusCacheMetadata(targetTag, true.B, false.B)

  dut.io.read.bits.tagIdx := targetSet
  dut.io.read.bits.validIdx := targetSet
  dut.io.read.bits.way_en := targetWay
  dut.io.read.bits.tag := targetTag

  switch(state) {
    is(sWrite) {
      dut.io.write.valid := true.B
      when(dut.io.write.ready) {
        state := sRead
      }
    }
    is(sRead) {
      dut.io.read.valid := true.B
      when(dut.io.read.ready) {
        state := sPrime
      }
    }
    is(sPrime) {
      when(!dut.io.resp(0).valid || dut.io.resp(0).error || dut.io.resp(0).tag =/= targetTag) {
        failedReg := true.B
      }
      state := sHold
    }
    is(sHold) {
      when(!dut.io.resp(0).valid || dut.io.resp(0).error || dut.io.resp(0).tag =/= targetTag) {
        failedReg := true.B
      }
      holdCycles := holdCycles + 1.U
      when(holdCycles === 7.U) {
        doneReg := true.B
        state := sDone
      }
    }
    is(sDone) {
      doneReg := true.B
    }
  }

  io.done := doneReg
  io.failed := failedReg
}

object Pr739Main extends App {
  XSParameters.set(XSParameters.debugParameters)
  XiangShanStage.execute(args, Seq(ChiselGeneratorAnnotation(() => new Pr739HoldReadReproTop)))
}
EOF

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's L1plusCache metadata array, a metadata read response can change or become invalid after the read has completed if downstream logic keeps using that response during later hold or stall cycles with no new read request. Instead of continuing to present the same tag and validity information, the array may lose or corrupt the metadata that was just returned. Expected behavior: after a metadata entry has been read successfully, the returned metadata response should remain stable and unchanged on subsequent hold cycles until a new metadata read replaces it. Affected function: L1plusCache metadata-array reads, which provide cache-line tag and valid/error state. Trigger condition: a metadata read is followed by one or more cycles with no new metadata SRAM read while consumers still rely on the previous response, especially on SRAM behavior that does not preserve old read data when read-enable is low.

mdp: use robIdx instead of sqIdx

dispatch queue. Yet we can still use "speculatively assigned" robIdx

but data it not valid. When load insts try to get forward data from
those store, load insts will get that stores's sqIdx and wait in RS.
They will not be wakeuped until store data with that sqIdx is issued.

@@ -0,0 +1,407 @@
+/***************************************************************************************

+
+package xiangshan.mem.mdp
+
+import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+import xiangshan._
+import utils._
+import xiangshan.backend.rob.RobPtr
+
+// store set load violation predictor
+// See "Memory Dependence Prediction using Store Sets" for details
+
+// Store Set Identifier Table Entry
+class SSITEntry(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val valid = Bool()
+  val ssid = UInt(SSIDWidth.W) // store set identifier
+  val strict = Bool() // strict load wait is needed
+}
+
+// Store Set Identifier Table Entry
+class SSITDataEntry(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val ssid = UInt(SSIDWidth.W) // store set identifier
+  val strict = Bool() // strict load wait is needed
+}
+
+// Store Set Identifier Table
+class SSIT(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    // to decode
+    val raddr = Vec(DecodeWidth, Input(UInt(MemPredPCWidth.W))) // xor hashed decode pc(VaddrBits-1, 1)
+    // to rename
+    val rdata = Vec(RenameWidth, Output(new SSITEntry))
+    // misc
+    val update = Input(new MemPredUpdateReq) // RegNext should be added outside
+    val csrCtrl = Input(new CustomCSRCtrlIO)
+  })
+
+  // raddrs are sent to ssit in decode
+  // rdata will be send to rename
+  require(DecodeWidth == RenameWidth)
+
+  // data sram read port allocate 
+  //
+  // SSIT update logic will reuse decode ssit read port.
+  // If io.update.valid, a redirect will be send to frontend,
+  // then decode will not need to read SSIT
+  val SSIT_DECODE_READ_PORT_BASE = 0
+  val SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT = 0
+  val SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT = 1
+  val SSIT_READ_PORT_NUM = DecodeWidth
+
+  // data sram write port allocate 
+  val SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT = 0
+  val SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT = 1
+  val SSIT_MISC_WRITE_PORT = 2
+  val SSIT_WRITE_PORT_NUM = 3
+
+  // TODO: reorg sram size
+  val valid_sram = Module(new SyncDataModuleTemplate(
+    Bool(),
+    SSITSize,
+    SSIT_READ_PORT_NUM,
+    SSIT_WRITE_PORT_NUM
+  ))
+
+  val data_sram = Module(new SyncDataModuleTemplate(
+    new SSITDataEntry,
+    SSITSize,
+    SSIT_READ_PORT_NUM,
+    SSIT_WRITE_PORT_NUM
+  ))
+
+  (0 until SSIT_WRITE_PORT_NUM).map(i => {
+    valid_sram.io.wen(i) := false.B
+    valid_sram.io.waddr(i) := DontCare
+    valid_sram.io.wdata(i) := DontCare
+    data_sram.io.wen(i) := false.B
+    data_sram.io.waddr(i) := DontCare
+    data_sram.io.wdata(i) := DontCare
+  })
+
+  val debug_valid = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(SSITSize)(false.B)))
+  val debug_ssid = Reg(Vec(SSITSize, UInt(SSIDWidth.W)))
+  val debug_strict = Reg(Vec(SSITSize, Bool()))
+  if(!env.FPGAPlatform){
+    dontTouch(debug_valid)
+    dontTouch(debug_ssid)
+    dontTouch(debug_strict)
+  }
+
+  val resetCounter = RegInit(0.U(ResetTimeMax2Pow.W))
+  resetCounter := resetCounter + 1.U
+
+  for (i <- 0 until DecodeWidth) {
+    // io.rdata(i).valid := RegNext(valid(io.raddr(i)))
+    // io.rdata(i).ssid := RegNext(ssid(io.raddr(i)))
+    // io.rdata(i).strict := RegNext(strict(io.raddr(i)) && valid(io.raddr(i)))
+
+    // read SSIT in decode stage
+    valid_sram.io.raddr(i) := io.raddr(i)
+    data_sram.io.raddr(i) := io.raddr(i)
+    
+    // gen result in rename stage
+    io.rdata(i).valid := valid_sram.io.rdata(i)
+    io.rdata(i).ssid := data_sram.io.rdata(i).ssid
+    io.rdata(i).strict := data_sram.io.rdata(i).strict
+  }
+
+  // update SSIT if load violation redirect is detected
+
+  // update stage 0: read ssit
+  val memPredUpdateReqValid = RegNext(io.update.valid)
+  val memPredUpdateReqReg = RegEnable(io.update, enable = io.update.valid)
+
+  // when io.update.valid, take over ssit read port
+  when (io.update.valid) {
+    valid_sram.io.raddr(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT) := io.update.ldpc
+    valid_sram.io.raddr(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT) := io.update.stpc
+    data_sram.io.raddr(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT) := io.update.ldpc
+    data_sram.io.raddr(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT) := io.update.stpc
+  }
+
+  // update stage 1: get ssit read result, update ssit data_sram
+
+  // Read result
+  // load has already been assigned with a store set
+  val loadAssigned = valid_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT)
+  val loadOldSSID = data_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT).ssid
+  val loadStrict = data_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT).strict
+  // store has already been assigned with a store set
+  val storeAssigned = valid_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT)
+  val storeOldSSID = data_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT).ssid
+  val storeStrict = data_sram.io.rdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_READ_PORT).strict
+  // both the load and the store have already been assigned store sets
+  // but load's store set ID is smaller
+  val winnerSSID = Mux(loadOldSSID < storeOldSSID, loadOldSSID, storeOldSSID)
+  val ssidIsSame = loadOldSSID === storeOldSSID
+
+  // for now we just use lowest bits of ldpc as store set id
+  val ssidAllocate = memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc(SSIDWidth-1, 0)
+
+  def update_ld_ssit_entry(pc: UInt, valid: Bool, ssid: UInt, strict: Bool) = {
+    valid_sram.io.wen(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT) := true.B
+    valid_sram.io.waddr(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT) := pc
+    valid_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT) := valid
+    data_sram.io.wen(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT) := true.B
+    data_sram.io.waddr(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT) := pc
+    data_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT).ssid := ssid
+    data_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_WRITE_PORT).strict := strict
+    debug_valid(pc) := valid
+    debug_ssid(pc) := ssid
+    debug_strict(pc) := strict 
+  }
+
+  def update_st_ssit_entry(pc: UInt, valid: Bool, ssid: UInt, strict: Bool) = {
+    valid_sram.io.wen(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT) := true.B
+    valid_sram.io.waddr(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT) := pc
+    valid_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT):= valid
+    data_sram.io.wen(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT) := true.B
+    data_sram.io.waddr(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT) := pc
+    data_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT).ssid := ssid
+    data_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_STORE_WRITE_PORT).strict := strict
+    debug_valid(pc) := valid
+    debug_ssid(pc) := ssid
+    debug_strict(pc) := strict 
+  }
+
+  // update stage 1
+  when(memPredUpdateReqValid){
+    switch (Cat(loadAssigned, storeAssigned)) {
+      // 1. "If neither the load nor the store has been assigned a store set,
+      // one is allocated and assigned to both instructions."
+      is ("b00".U(2.W)) {
+        update_ld_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = ssidAllocate,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+        update_st_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.stpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = ssidAllocate,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+      }
+      // 2. "If the load has been assigned a store set, but the store has not,
+      // the store is assigned the load’s store set."
+      is ("b10".U(2.W)) {
+        update_st_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.stpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = loadOldSSID,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+      }
+      // 3. "If the store has been assigned a store set, but the load has not,
+      // the load is assigned the store’s store set."
+      is ("b01".U(2.W)) {
+        update_ld_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = storeOldSSID,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+      }
+      // 4. "If both the load and the store have already been assigned store sets,
+      // one of the two store sets is declared the "winner".
+      // The instruction belonging to the loser’s store set is assigned the winner’s store set."
+      is ("b11".U(2.W)) {
+        update_ld_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = winnerSSID,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+        update_st_ssit_entry(
+          pc = memPredUpdateReqReg.stpc,
+          valid = true.B,
+          ssid = winnerSSID,
+          strict = false.B
+        )
+        when(ssidIsSame){
+          data_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_UPDATE_LOAD_READ_PORT).strict := true.B
+          debug_strict(memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc) := false.B
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_lxsx", memPredUpdateReqValid && !loadAssigned && !storeAssigned)
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_lysx", memPredUpdateReqValid && loadAssigned && !storeAssigned)
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_lxsy", memPredUpdateReqValid && !loadAssigned && storeAssigned)
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_lysy", memPredUpdateReqValid && loadAssigned && storeAssigned)
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_should_strict", memPredUpdateReqValid && ssidIsSame && loadAssigned && storeAssigned)
+  XSPerfAccumulate("ssit_update_strict_failed", 
+    memPredUpdateReqValid && ssidIsSame && loadStrict && loadAssigned && storeAssigned
+  ) // should be zero
+
+  // reset period: ResetTimeMax2Pow
+  val resetStepCounter = RegInit(0.U((log2Up(SSITSize)+1).W))
+  val resetStepCounterFull = resetStepCounter(log2Up(SSITSize))
+  val s_idle :: s_flush :: Nil = Enum(2)
+  val state = RegInit(s_flush)
+
+  switch (state) {
+    is(s_idle) {
+      when(resetCounter(ResetTimeMax2Pow-1, ResetTimeMin2Pow)(RegNext(io.csrCtrl.lvpred_timeout))) {
+        state := s_flush
+        resetCounter := 0.U
+      }
+    }
+    is(s_flush) {
+      when(resetStepCounterFull) {
+        state := s_idle // reset finished
+        resetStepCounter := 0.U
+      }.otherwise{
+        valid_sram.io.wen(SSIT_MISC_WRITE_PORT) := true.B
+        valid_sram.io.waddr(SSIT_MISC_WRITE_PORT) := resetStepCounter
+        valid_sram.io.wdata(SSIT_MISC_WRITE_PORT) := false.B
+        debug_valid(resetStepCounter) := false.B
+        resetStepCounter := resetStepCounter + 1.U
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  // debug
+  for (i <- 0 until StorePipelineWidth) {
+    when (memPredUpdateReqReg.valid) {
+      XSDebug("%d: SSIT update: load pc %x store pc %x\n", GTimer(), memPredUpdateReqReg.ldpc, memPredUpdateReqReg.stpc)
+      XSDebug("%d: SSIT update: load valid %b ssid %x  store valid %b ssid %x\n", GTimer(), loadAssigned, loadOldSSID, storeAssigned, storeOldSSID)
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+
+// Last Fetched Store Table Entry
+class LFSTEntry(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle  {
+  val valid = Bool()
+  val robIdx = new RobPtr
+}
+
+class LFSTReq(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val isstore = Bool()
+  val ssid = UInt(SSIDWidth.W) // use ssid to lookup LFST
+  val robIdx = new RobPtr
+}
+
+class LFSTResp(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val shouldWait = Bool()
+  val robIdx = new RobPtr
+}
+
+class DispatchLFSTIO(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSBundle {
+  val req = Vec(RenameWidth, Valid(new LFSTReq))
+  val resp = Vec(RenameWidth, Flipped(Valid(new LFSTResp)))
+}
+
+// Last Fetched Store Table
+class LFST(implicit p: Parameters) extends XSModule {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    // when redirect, mark canceled store as invalid
+    val redirect = Input(Valid(new Redirect))
+    val dispatch = Flipped(new DispatchLFSTIO)
+    // when store issued, mark store as invalid
+    val storeIssue = Vec(exuParameters.StuCnt, Flipped(Valid(new ExuInput)))
+    val csrCtrl = Input(new CustomCSRCtrlIO)
+  })
+
+  val validVec = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(LFSTSize)(VecInit(Seq.fill(LFSTWidth)(false.B)))))
+  val robIdxVec = Reg(Vec(LFSTSize, Vec(LFSTWidth, new RobPtr)))
+  val allocPtr = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(LFSTSize)(0.U(log2Up(LFSTWidth).W))))
+  val valid = Wire(Vec(LFSTSize, Bool()))
+  (0 until LFSTSize).map(i => {
+    valid(i) := validVec(i).asUInt.orR
+  })
+
+  // read LFST in rename stage
+  for (i <- 0 until RenameWidth) {
+    io.dispatch.resp(i).valid := io.dispatch.req(i).valid
+
+    // If store-load pair is in the same dispatch bundle, loadWaitBit should also be set for load
+    val hitInDispatchBundleVec = if(i > 0){
+      WireInit(VecInit((0 until i).map(j =>
+        io.dispatch.req(j).valid &&
+        io.dispatch.req(j).bits.isstore &&
+        io.dispatch.req(j).bits.ssid === io.dispatch.req(i).bits.ssid
+      )))
+    } else {
+      WireInit(VecInit(Seq(false.B))) // DontCare
+    }
+    val hitInDispatchBundle = hitInDispatchBundleVec.asUInt.orR
+    // Check if store set is valid in LFST
+    io.dispatch.resp(i).bits.shouldWait := (
+        (valid(io.dispatch.req(i).bits.ssid) || hitInDispatchBundle) && 
+        io.dispatch.req(i).valid &&
+        (!io.dispatch.req(i).bits.isstore || io.csrCtrl.storeset_wait_store)
+      ) && !io.csrCtrl.lvpred_disable || io.csrCtrl.no_spec_load
+    io.dispatch.resp(i).bits.robIdx := robIdxVec(io.dispatch.req(i).bits.ssid)(allocPtr(io.dispatch.req(i).bits.ssid)-1.U)
+    if(i > 0){
+      (0 until i).map(j =>
+        when(hitInDispatchBundleVec(j)){
+          io.dispatch.resp(i).bits.robIdx := io.dispatch.req(i).bits.robIdx
+        }
+      )
+    }
+  }
+
+  // when store is issued, mark it as invalid
+  (0 until exuParameters.StuCnt).map(i => {
+    // TODO: opt timing
+    (0 until LFSTWidth).map(j => {
+      when(io.storeIssue(i).valid && io.storeIssue(i).bits.uop.robIdx.value === robIdxVec(io.storeIssue(i).bits.uop.cf.ssid)(j).value){
+        validVec(io.storeIssue(i).bits.uop.cf.ssid)(j) := false.B
+      }
+    })
+  })
+
+  // when store is dispatched, mark it as valid
+  (0 until RenameWidth).map(i => {
+    when(io.dispatch.req(i).valid && io.dispatch.req(i).bits.isstore){
+      val waddr = io.dispatch.req(i).bits.ssid
+      val wptr = allocPtr(waddr)
+      allocPtr(waddr) := allocPtr(waddr) + 1.U
+      validVec(waddr)(wptr) := true.B
+      robIdxVec(waddr)(wptr) := io.dispatch.req(i).bits.robIdx
+    }
+  })
+
+  // when redirect, cancel store influenced
+  (0 until LFSTSize).map(i => {
+    (0 until LFSTWidth).map(j => {
+      when(robIdxVec(i)(j).needFlush(io.redirect)){
+        validVec(i)(j) := false.B
+      }
+    })
+  })
+
+  // recover robIdx after squash
+  // behavior model, to be refactored later 
+  when(RegNext(io.redirect.fire())) {
+    (0 until LFSTSize).map(i => {
+      (0 until LFSTWidth).map(j => {
+        val check_position = WireInit(allocPtr(i) + (j+1).U)
+        when(!validVec(i)(check_position)){
+          allocPtr(i) := check_position
+        }
+      })
+    })
+  }
+}

package mdptest

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util.log2Up
import chiseltest._
import chiseltest.ChiselScalatestTester
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec

import top.MinimalConfig
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.backend.issue.{RSParams, StatusArray, StatusEntry}
import xiangshan.backend.rob.RobPtr
import xiangshan.mem.SqPtr

class StatusArrayStoreSetWakeHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  private val coreParams = p(XSCoreParamsKey)
  private val rsParams = RSParams(
    numEntries = 1,
    numEnq = 1,
    numDeq = 1,
    numSrc = 1,
    dataBits = coreParams.XLEN,
    dataIdBits = log2Up(coreParams.NRPhyRegs),
    numFastWakeup = 0,
    numWakeup = 1,
    hasFeedback = false,
    delayedRf = false,
    fixedLatency = -1,
    checkWaitBit = true,
    optBuf = false,
    exuCfg = Some(AluExeUnitCfg)
  )

  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val enqueue = Input(Bool())
    val loadSqIdx = Input(new SqPtr)
    val waitSqIdx = Input(new SqPtr)
    val waitRobIdx = Input(new RobPtr)
    val stIssuePtr = Input(new SqPtr)
    val issueValid = Input(Bool())
    val issueSqIdx = Input(new SqPtr)
    val issueRobIdx = Input(new RobPtr)
    val canIssue = Output(Bool())
  })

  val dut = Module(new StatusArray(rsParams))

  private def assignIfPresent(record: Record, name: String, value: Data): Unit = {
    record.elements.get(name).foreach { field =>
      field := value.asUInt.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(field))
    }
  }

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new Redirect)

  dut.io.wakeup(0).valid := false.B
  dut.io.wakeup(0).bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MicroOp)

  dut.io.issueGranted(0).valid := false.B
  dut.io.issueGranted(0).bits := 0.U

  dut.io.updateMidState := 0.U

  dut.io.deqResp(0).valid := false.B
  dut.io.deqResp(0).bits.rsMask := 0.U
  dut.io.deqResp(0).bits.success := false.B
  dut.io.deqResp(0).bits.resptype := 0.U
  dut.io.deqResp(0).bits.dataInvalidSqIdx := 0.U.asTypeOf(new SqPtr)

  dut.io.stIssuePtr := io.stIssuePtr

  for (i <- 0 until dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue.length) {
    dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue(i).valid := false.B
    dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue(i).bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new ExuInput)
    dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.stdIssue(i).valid := false.B
    dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.stdIssue(i).bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new ExuInput)
  }

  dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue(0).valid := io.issueValid
  dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue(0).bits.uop.sqIdx := io.issueSqIdx
  dut.io.memWaitUpdateReq.staIssue(0).bits.uop.robIdx := io.issueRobIdx

  val entry = WireInit(0.U.asTypeOf(new StatusEntry(rsParams)))
  entry.valid := true.B
  entry.scheduled := false.B
  entry.blocked := true.B
  entry.credit := 0.U
  entry.srcState(0) := true.B
  entry.midState := false.B
  entry.psrc(0) := 0.U
  entry.srcType(0) := SrcType.reg
  entry.robIdx := 0.U.asTypeOf(new RobPtr)
  entry.waitForSqIdx := io.waitSqIdx
  assignIfPresent(entry, "waitForRobIdx", io.waitRobIdx)
  entry.waitForStoreData := false.B
  entry.strictWait := false.B
  entry.sqIdx := io.loadSqIdx
  entry.isFirstIssue := true.B

  dut.io.update(0).enable := io.enqueue
  dut.io.update(0).addr := 1.U
  dut.io.update(0).data := entry

  io.canIssue := dut.io.canIssue(0)
}

class StatusArrayStoreSetWakeupBenchTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "StatusArray"

  it should "wake a blocked load when the matching store issue arrives" in {
    implicit val p: Parameters = new MinimalConfig(1).alter((site, here, up) => {
      case XSCoreParamsKey => up(XSTileKey).head
    })

    test(new StatusArrayStoreSetWakeHarness) { dut =>
      dut.io.enqueue.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.issueValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.stIssuePtr.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.stIssuePtr.value.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.loadSqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.loadSqIdx.value.poke(3.U)
      dut.io.waitSqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.waitSqIdx.value.poke(2.U)
      dut.io.waitRobIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.waitRobIdx.value.poke(1.U)
      dut.io.issueSqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.issueSqIdx.value.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.issueRobIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.issueRobIdx.value.poke(0.U)

      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.enqueue.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.enqueue.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.canIssue.expect(false.B)

      dut.io.issueSqIdx.value.poke(1.U)
      dut.io.issueRobIdx.value.poke(1.U)
      dut.io.issueValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.issueValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.canIssue.expect(true.B)
    }
  }
}
EOF

set +e
timeout 1200 env JAVA_HOME="$JAVA_HOME" PATH="$PATH" MILL_VERSION="$MILL_VERSION" \
  "$mill_cmd" -i XiangShan.test.testOnly mdptest.StatusArrayStoreSetWakeupBenchTest \
  2>&1 | tee /home/xiangshan/statusarray_store_set_wakeup.log
test_status=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [[ $test_status -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "TEST: statusarray_store_set_wakeup ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: statusarray_store_set_wakeup ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$test_status"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's Control and Status Register (CSR) unit, writing `mstatus` with the `XS` bits set changes the read-only extension-status state (`xstatus.xs`), so a subsequent `mstatus` read can report non-zero `XS` and set `SD`. A write to `satp` can also preserve `PPN` bits above the implementation's supported physical-address width. Expected behavior: software writes must not modify the read-only `XS` field, so `mstatus` readback should leave `XS` unchanged and should not set `SD` because of that write. `satp.ppn` should be limited to the implemented physical-page-number width and discard unsupported high bits on readback. Affected function: CSR read/write handling for `mstatus`/`xstatus` and `satp` in XiangShan. Trigger condition: the bug appears when software writes `mstatus` with `XS` bits set, or writes `satp` with high `PPN` bits set on configurations whose physical address width is narrower than the architectural `satp.ppn` field.

Exception address is used serveral cycles after flush. We delay it
by more cycles to ensure its flush safety.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/MemBlock.scala b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/MemBlock.scala
index 6ae3c3ab280..cff30d1f21f 100644
--- a/src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/MemBlock.scala
+++ b/src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/MemBlock.scala
@@ -517,7 +517,12 @@ class MemBlockImp(outer: MemBlock) extends LazyModuleImp(outer)
   lsq.io.exceptionAddr.isStore := io.lsqio.exceptionAddr.isStore
   // Exception address is used serveral cycles after flush.
   // We delay it by 10 cycles to ensure its flush safety.
-  val atomicsException = DelayN(atomicsUnit.io.exceptionAddr.valid, 10)
+  val atomicsException = RegInit(false.B)
+  when (DelayN(io.redirect.valid, 10) && atomicsException) {
+    atomicsException := false.B
+  }.elsewhen (atomicsUnit.io.exceptionAddr.valid) {
+    atomicsException := true.B
+  }
   val atomicsExceptionAddress = RegEnable(atomicsUnit.io.exceptionAddr.bits, atomicsUnit.io.exceptionAddr.valid)
   io.lsqio.exceptionAddr.vaddr := Mux(atomicsException, atomicsExceptionAddress, lsq.io.exceptionAddr.vaddr)
   XSError(atomicsException && atomicsUnit.io.in.valid, "new instruction before exception triggers\n")

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's backend MemBlock, an atomic memory exception can stop being reported on the LSQ (load/store queue) exception-address output before the saved exception address is consumed. This means logic that reads the address several cycles later can miss the atomic exception address even though the exception is still pending. Expected behavior: once an atomic exception is raised, MemBlock should keep that exception address visible on the LSQ exception-address output across later cycles, so a consumer that samples it several cycles after the flush still sees the same address; the latched atomic exception should only be cleared when the later redirect/flush handling for that exception takes effect. Affected function: MemBlock logic that latches and forwards atomic exception addresses to the LSQ exception-address interface. Trigger condition: an atomic memory operation raises an exception, and the exception address is consumed several cycles later instead of immediately.

title: mem: reduce refill to use latency
body:
This commit updates lq entry flag carefully in load_s3 to avoid extra
refill delay. It removes the extra refill delay introduced by #1375
without harming memblock timing.

In #1375, we delayed load refill when dcache miss queue entry fails
to accept a miss. It exchanged performance for better timing.

commits.message:
mem: optimize missq reject to lq timing

DCache replay request is quite slow to generate, as it need to compare
load address with address in all valid miss queue entries.

Now we delay the usage of replay request from data cache.
Now replay request will not influence normal execuation flow until
load_s3 (1 cycle after load_s2, load result writeback to RS).

It is worth mentioning that "select refilling inst for load
writeback" will be disabled if dcacheRequireReplay in the
last cycle.
dcache: compare probe block addr instead of full addr

mem: do not replay from RS when ldld vio or fwd failed

ld-ld violation or forward failure will let an normal load inst replay
from fetch. If TLB hit and ld-ld violation / forward failure happens,
we write back that inst immediately. Meanwhile, such insts will not be
replayed from rs.

It should fix "mem: optimize missq reject to lq timing"
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into timing-memblock-211203
mem: fix replay from rs condition
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into timing-memblock-211203

    git -C "$path" config --local --add url.https://github.com/.insteadOf git://github.com/ || true

    git -C "$path" submodule sync --recursive || true
    git -C "$path" submodule update --init --recursive || true

}

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's load pipeline, a load that is rejected by the DCache miss queue/MSHR is marked for replay from the reservation station (RS). If a matching refill, meaning the returning cache-line data for that miss, arrives before the replay is reissued, the slow replay feedback still reports the load as needing replay, which adds an unnecessary extra refill-to-use delay. Expected behavior: when a refill for the same load address arrives in that window, the load should be treated as satisfied by the refill and the slow replay feedback should report it as a hit instead of forcing another replay. Affected function: LoadUnit slow replay feedback for miss-queue reject cases in the memory subsystem. Trigger condition: a load issues, the DCache cannot accept its miss request, and a refill for the same load address arrives before the replayed load is sent again.

* dcache: do not access plru when refill

Now we have accessed plru when load miss, we should not access plru
when refill

* dcache: not not access plru when miss queue full

It will help avoid invalid plru access when miss queue full

This commit re-pipelines ECC check logic in data cache and exception generate logic for better timing.
Now ecc error is checked 1 cycle after reading result from data sram. An extra cycle is added for load
writeback to ROB.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan
source /etc/xiangshan_tools_path.sh 2>/dev/null || true
export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64}"
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export MILL_VERSION="${MILL_VERSION:-0.9.8}"

mkdir -p src/test/scala/xiangshan
cat > src/test/scala/xiangshan/Wb2CtrlLoadDelaySpec.scala <<'EOF'
package xiangshan

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import freechips.rocketchip.diplomacy.{LazyModule, LazyModuleImp}
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers
import top.BaseConfig
import xiangshan.backend.exu.Wb2Ctrl

class Wb2CtrlLoadDelayWrapper(implicit p: Parameters) extends LazyModule {
  val inner = LazyModule(new Wb2Ctrl(Seq(LdExeUnitCfg)))

  lazy val module = new LazyModuleImp(this) {
    val io = IO(new Bundle {
      val inValid = Input(Bool())
      val outValid = Output(Bool())
    })

    inner.module.io.redirect.valid := false.B
    inner.module.io.redirect.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new Redirect)
    inner.module.io.in(0).valid := io.inValid
    inner.module.io.in(0).ready := true.B
    inner.module.io.in(0).bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new ExuOutput)
    inner.module.io.elements.get("delayedLoadError").foreach { data =>
      data.asInstanceOf[Vec[Bool]].foreach(_ := false.B)
    }

    io.outValid := inner.module.io.out(0).valid
  }
}

class Wb2CtrlLoadDelaySpec extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "Wb2Ctrl load writeback timing"

  it should "delay load writeback by one cycle" in {
    implicit val p: Parameters = new BaseConfig(1).alterPartial {
      case XSCoreParamsKey => XSCoreParameters(HartId = 0)
    }
    test(LazyModule(new Wb2CtrlLoadDelayWrapper).module) { dut =>
      dut.io.inValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)

      dut.io.inValid.poke(true.B)
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()

      dut.io.outValid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.inValid.poke(false.B)
      dut.clock.step()
      dut.io.outValid.expect(false.B)
    }
  }
}
EOF

log_file="/home/xiangshan/wb2ctrl_load_delay.log"

if timeout 1200s env MILL_VERSION="$MILL_VERSION" /usr/local/bin/mill --no-server \

else

fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
echo "TEST: ${test_name} ... ${result}"
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$status"

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in the Nanhu load/store unit (LSU), after the data-cache ECC/error check was moved one cycle later for timing, a load could still be reported as written back in the original cycle. This means load completion can be signaled before the final result of the delayed error check is available. Expected behavior: any load on this repipelined data-cache path must write back to the reorder buffer (ROB) one cycle later, so completion is reported only after the delayed ECC/error stage, even when the load ultimately has no error. Affected function: the LSU/data-cache load writeback timing path to ROB writeback. Trigger condition: loads that use the data-cache path after ECC/error checking has been repipelined to occur one cycle after the data SRAM read.

title: rob: fix commitInstr performance counters
body:
This commit fixes the wrong update values of commitInstr in ROB.
Previously we add a RegNext to trueCommitCnt in #1644. However,
we don't add RegNext to the ifCommit condition. This makes the
commitInstr larger than the normal value and IPC looks better.

This commit fixes this bug and the IPC numbers should be correct now.

commits.message:
rob: fix commitInstr performance counters

This commit fixes the wrong update values of commitInstr in ROB.
Previously we add a RegNext to trueCommitCnt in #1644. However,
we don't add RegNext to the ifCommit condition. This makes the
commitInstr larger than the normal value and IPC looks better.

This commit fixes this bug and the IPC numbers should be correct now.

problem_statement: The backend reorder buffer (ROB) uses the `commitInstr` performance counter to report how many instructions retire. After the timing optimization introduced in #1644, this accounting can overcount retirements: during a single-instruction commit sequence, `commitInstr` may increment twice even though only one instruction actually commits, which makes IPC appear higher than it is. Expected behavior: each committed instruction must contribute exactly one to `commitInstr`, so a one-instruction commit sequence produces a `commitInstr` increment of one and IPC matches the true retirement rate. Affected function: ROB retirement performance accounting, specifically `commitInstr`. Trigger condition: this occurs when the ROB's commit accounting uses commit-count information and the commit-valid decision from different cycles after the #1644 timing change, causing the same retirement sequence to be charged again.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's load unit, a load that should be reissued from the fetch side (`replay_from_fetch`) can lose that replay state when its load-queue entry is updated on a miss-path cycle. In the verified scenario, the load reaches the data-cache response stage, sees a data-cache miss together with an invalid forwarding match, and should stay marked as replay-from-fetch rather than taking a normal completion path. Expected behavior: once the load pipeline decides that a load must replay from fetch, the load-queue update for that instruction must preserve that replay state even on the miss path. After the miss-plus-invalid-forwarding case, the following stage must still report replay-from-fetch, and the load must not be emitted as a normal completed load. Affected function: replay-from-fetch handling in the load unit / load-queue update path. Trigger condition: a load reaches the data-cache response path and encounters the verified replay-from-fetch case of a data-cache miss combined with an invalid forwarding match.

body: timing modification of #1681

commits.message:
ldu: optimize dcache hitvec wiring

In previous design, hitvec is generated in load s1, then send to dcache
and lsu (rs) side separately. As dcache and lsu (rs side) is far in real
chip, it caused severe wiring problem.

Now we generate 2 hitvec in parallel:

* hitvec 1 is generated near dcache.
To generate that signal, paddr from dtlb is sent to dcache in load_s1
to geerate hitvec. The hitvec is then sent to dcache to generate
data array read_way_en.

* hitvec 2 is generated near lsu and rs in load_s2, tag read result
from dcache, as well as coh_state, is sent to lsu in load_s1,
then it is used to calcuate hitvec in load_s2.  hitvec 2 is used
to generate hit/miss signal used by lsu.

It should fix the wiring problem caused by hitvec

ldu: opt loadViolationQuery.resp.ready timing

An extra release addr register is added near lsu to speed up the
generation of loadViolationQuery.resp.ready

l1tlb: replace NormalPage data module and add duplicate resp result

data module:
add BankedSyncDataMoudleWithDup data module:
divided the data array into banks and read as Async, bypass write data.
RegNext the data result * #banks. choose from the chosen data.

duplicate:
duplicate the chosen data and return to outside(tlb).
tlb return (ppn+perm) * #DUP to outside (for load unit only)

TODO: load unit use different tlb resp result to different module.
one for lsq, one for dcache.

l1tlb: Fix wrong vidx_bypass logic after using duplicate data module

We use BankedSyncDataMoudleWithDup instead of SyncDataModuleTemplate,
whose write ports are not Vec.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/xiangshan

TEST_NAME="loadunit_fast_wakeup_on_miss"
SCALA_DIR="/home/xiangshan/src/test/scala/hwebench"
SCALA_FILE="${SCALA_DIR}/LoadUnitFastWakeupMain.scala"
CPP_FILE="/home/xiangshan/tmp_LoadUnitFastWakeup_main.cpp"
BUILD_DIR="/home/xiangshan/build/hwe-loadunit-fastwakeup"
OBJ_DIR="/home/xiangshan/obj_dir"
TOP_NAME="LoadUnitFastWakeupHarness"

write_reproducer_sources() {
  mkdir -p "${SCALA_DIR}"

  cat > "${SCALA_FILE}" <<'EOF'
package hwebench

import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import chisel3._
import chisel3.stage.ChiselStage
import top.MinimalConfig
import xiangshan._
import xiangshan.mem.LoadUnit

class LoadUnitFastWakeupHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(new Bundle {
    val fastWakeupSeen = Output(Bool())
    val missSeen = Output(Bool())
  })

  val dut = Module(new LoadUnit)
  val cycle = RegInit(0.U(4.W))
  cycle := cycle + 1.U

  def zeroOf[T <: Data](target: T): T = 0.U.asTypeOf(chiselTypeOf(target))

  def setUIntLike(target: Data, value: UInt): Unit = target match {
    case field: UInt => field := value
    case vec: Vec[_] => vec.foreach(_.asInstanceOf[UInt] := value)
    case other => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"unsupported UInt-like target: ${other.getClass}")
  }

  def setBoolLike(target: Data, value: Bool): Unit = target match {
    case field: Bool => field := value
    case vec: Vec[_] => vec.foreach(_.asInstanceOf[Bool] := value)
    case other => throw new IllegalArgumentException(s"unsupported Bool-like target: ${other.getClass}")
  }

  def recordField(target: Data, name: String): Option[Data] = target match {
    case record: Record => record.elements.get(name)
    case _ => None
  }

  val loadIn = WireInit(zeroOf(dut.io.ldin.bits))
  loadIn.src(0) := "h8000_0000".U
  loadIn.uop.ctrl.fuOpType := LSUOpType.ld
  loadIn.uop.ctrl.imm := 0.U
  loadIn.uop.cf.pc := "h1000".U

  dut.io.ldin.valid := cycle === 0.U
  dut.io.ldin.bits := loadIn
  dut.io.ldout.ready := true.B

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirect.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.redirect.bits)
  dut.io.rsIdx := 0.U
  dut.io.isFirstIssue := true.B

  dut.io.fastpathIn := zeroOf(dut.io.fastpathIn)
  dut.io.loadFastMatch := false.B
  dut.io.loadFastImm := 0.U

  dut.io.tlb.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.tlb.resp.valid := cycle === 1.U
  dut.io.tlb.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits)
  recordField(dut.io.tlb.resp.bits, "paddr").foreach(setUIntLike(_, "h8000_0000".U))

  dut.io.pmp := zeroOf(dut.io.pmp)

  dut.io.dcache.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.valid := cycle === 2.U
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.dcache.resp.bits)
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.miss := true.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.replay := false.B
  dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.tag_error := false.B

  val dcacheIo = dut.io.dcache.asInstanceOf[Record]
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_hit_way").foreach(setUIntLike(_, 1.U))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("debug_s1_hit_way").foreach(setUIntLike(_, 1.U))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s2_hit").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_disable_fast_wakeup").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))
  dcacheIo.elements.get("s1_bank_conflict").foreach(setBoolLike(_, false.B))

  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardMaskFast.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardMask.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.sbuffer.forwardData.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  dut.io.sbuffer.dataInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.sbuffer.matchInvalid := false.B

  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardMaskFast.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardMask.foreach(_ := false.B)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.forwardData.foreach(_ := 0.U)
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalidFast := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.matchInvalid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.forward.dataInvalidSqIdx := 0.U

  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.req.ready := true.B
  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.loadViolationQuery.resp.bits)

  dut.io.lsq.ldout.valid := false.B
  dut.io.lsq.ldout.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.lsq.ldout.bits)

  dut.io.lsq.trigger.lqLoadAddrTriggerHitVec.foreach(_ := false.B)

  dut.io.refill.valid := false.B
  dut.io.refill.bits := zeroOf(dut.io.refill.bits)

  dut.io.csrCtrl := zeroOf(dut.io.csrCtrl)

  dut.io.trigger.foreach { trigger =>
    trigger.tdata2 := 0.U
    trigger.matchType := 0.U
    trigger.tEnable := false.B
  }

  io.fastWakeupSeen := dut.io.fastUop.valid
  io.missSeen := dut.io.dcache.resp.valid && dut.io.dcache.resp.bits.miss

  when (cycle === 2.U && dut.io.dcache.resp.valid) {
    assert(!dut.io.fastUop.valid, "fast wakeup must stay low when the dcache response is a miss")
  }

  when (cycle === 5.U) {
    stop()
  }
}

object LoadUnitFastWakeupMain extends App {
  val targetDir = if (args.nonEmpty) args(0) else "build/hwe-loadunit-fastwakeup"
  val baseConfig = new MinimalConfig(1)
  val standaloneConfig = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head
  }
  (new ChiselStage).emitVerilog(
    gen = new LoadUnitFastWakeupHarness()(standaloneConfig),
    args = Array("--target-dir", targetDir)
  )
}
EOF

  cat > "${CPP_FILE}" <<'EOF'
#include "VLoadUnitFastWakeupHarness.h"
#include "verilated.h"

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  Verilated::commandArgs(argc, argv);
  VLoadUnitFastWakeupHarness top;

  for (int cycle = 0; cycle < 12 && !Verilated::gotFinish(); ++cycle) {
    top.reset = cycle < 2;
    top.clock = 0;
    top.eval();
    top.clock = 1;
    top.eval();
  }

  top.final();
  return Verilated::gotFinish() ? 0 : 1;
}
EOF
}

run_reproducer() {
  write_reproducer_sources

  rm -rf "${BUILD_DIR}" "${OBJ_DIR}"

  export JAVA_HOME="${JAVA_HOME:-/usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64}"
  export PATH="${JAVA_HOME}/bin:/tools/bin:/tools/mill/bin:${PATH}"
  if [ -f /home/xiangshan/.mill-version ]; then
    export MILL_VERSION="$(tr -d ' \t\r\n' < /home/xiangshan/.mill-version)"
  else
    export MILL_VERSION="0.9.8"
  fi
  if [ -x /usr/local/bin/install-mill-version ]; then
    /usr/local/bin/install-mill-version "${MILL_VERSION}" >/dev/null
  fi

  /usr/local/bin/mill -i XiangShan.test.runMain hwebench.LoadUnitFastWakeupMain "${BUILD_DIR}" &&
    VERILATOR_ROOT="/tools/v4.210/share/verilator" \
    VERILATOR_BIN="../../bin/verilator_bin" \
    /tools/v4.210/bin/verilator --assert --cc "${BUILD_DIR}/${TOP_NAME}.v" \
      --exe "${CPP_FILE}" --build &&
    "${OBJ_DIR}/V${TOP_NAME}"
}

if run_reproducer; then
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 0
else
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 1
fi
problem_statement: In XiangShan, the load/store unit (LSU) generates a fast wakeup signal to let dependent instructions proceed early when a load hits in the data cache (DCache). The bug is that this fast wakeup decision can follow an earlier cache hit indication instead of the LSU-visible DCache hit result for the same load. Under the trigger condition where a load sees an early hit-way or tag-match indication but the later DCache result is actually a miss, the LSU may still assert fast wakeup. The affected function is the LoadUnit fast-wakeup generation for DCache loads. The expected behavior is specific: fast wakeup must only be asserted for a confirmed DCache hit, and it must remain low whenever the DCache result is a miss.

package xiangshan.mem.mdp

import chisel3._
import chiseltest._
import chipsalliance.rocketchip.config.Parameters
import org.scalatest.flatspec.AnyFlatSpec
import org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers
import top.MinimalConfig
import xiangshan._

class LFSTHarness(implicit p: Parameters) extends Module {
  val io = IO(Flipped(new DispatchLFSTIO))

  val dut = Module(new LFST)
  dut.io.dispatch <> io

  dut.io.redirect.valid := false.B
  dut.io.redirect.bits := DontCare

  dut.io.storeIssue.foreach { issue =>
    issue.valid := false.B
    issue.bits := DontCare
  }

  dut.io.csrCtrl := DontCare
  dut.io.csrCtrl.lvpred_disable := false.B
  dut.io.csrCtrl.no_spec_load := false.B
  dut.io.csrCtrl.storeset_wait_store := false.B
  dut.io.csrCtrl.lvpred_timeout := 0.U
}

class LFSTRegressionTest extends AnyFlatSpec with ChiselScalatestTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "LFST"

  private val baseConfig = new MinimalConfig()
  implicit val p: Parameters = baseConfig.alterPartial {
    case XSCoreParamsKey => baseConfig(XSTileKey).head
  }
  private val renameWidth = p(XSCoreParamsKey).RenameWidth

  require(renameWidth >= 2, s"LFST regression test requires RenameWidth >= 2, got $renameWidth")

  private def clearReqs(dut: LFSTHarness): Unit = {
    for (slot <- 0 until renameWidth) {
      dut.io.req(slot).valid.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.isstore.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.ssid.poke(0.U)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
      dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.value.poke(0.U)
    }
  }

  private def pokeReq(
    dut: LFSTHarness,
    slot: Int,
    isStore: Boolean,
    ssid: Int,
    robValue: Int,
    robFlag: Boolean = false
  ): Unit = {
    dut.io.req(slot).valid.poke(true.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.isstore.poke(isStore.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.ssid.poke(ssid.U)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.poke(robFlag.B)
    dut.io.req(slot).bits.robIdx.value.poke(robValue.U)
  }

  private def expectRobIdx(dut: LFSTHarness, slot: Int, robValue: Int, robFlag: Boolean = false): Unit = {
    dut.io.resp(slot).bits.robIdx.flag.expect(robFlag.B)
    dut.io.resp(slot).bits.robIdx.value.expect(robValue.U)
  }

  it should "return the older same-bundle store robIdx for a dependent load" in {
    test(new LFSTHarness) { dut =>
      clearReqs(dut)

      pokeReq(dut, slot = 0, isStore = true, ssid = 5, robValue = 3)
      pokeReq(dut, slot = 1, isStore = false, ssid = 5, robValue = 9)

      dut.io.resp(0).valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.resp(0).bits.shouldWait.expect(false.B)
      dut.io.resp(1).valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.resp(1).bits.shouldWait.expect(true.B)
      expectRobIdx(dut, slot = 1, robValue = 3)
    }
  }

  it should "remember the store robIdx from the correct dispatch slot" in {
    test(new LFSTHarness) { dut =>
      clearReqs(dut)

      pokeReq(dut, slot = 0, isStore = true, ssid = 1, robValue = 2)
      pokeReq(dut, slot = 1, isStore = true, ssid = 7, robValue = 13)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearReqs(dut)
      pokeReq(dut, slot = 0, isStore = false, ssid = 7, robValue = 21)

      dut.io.resp(0).valid.expect(true.B)
      dut.io.resp(0).bits.shouldWait.expect(true.B)
      expectRobIdx(dut, slot = 0, robValue = 13)
    }
  }
}
EOF

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's memory dependence predictor (MDP), the LFST/StoreSet logic uses a StoreSet ID (SSID) to remember the reorder-buffer (ROB) index of the older store that a load should wait for. When multiple instructions are dispatched together, this lookup can return the wrong ROB index. A load that follows an older store with the same SSID in the same dispatch bundle can be predicted as waiting on its own ROB entry, and if multiple stores are dispatched together, a later load can receive the ROB index from the wrong store. Expected behavior: for a load that matches an older store by SSID, the LFST response must indicate that the load should wait and must return the ROB index of that matching older store, never the load's own ROB index or the ROB index of an unrelated store. Affected function: the LFST/StoreSet logic in XiangShan's MDP. Trigger condition: dispatching multiple instructions in one group, especially a same-SSID store and load in the same bundle or multiple stores followed by a load that queries one of their SSIDs.

problem_statement: Observed behavior: In XiangShan's CtrlBlock, a frontend instruction can still enter decode during the brief window after a flush-after redirect has been raised but is still pending. If that wrong-path instruction is a `vset*` instruction, it incorrectly updates the vector configuration state used by later vector instructions, so the next correct-path vector instruction is dispatched with the wrong `vconfig`. Expected behavior: Once a flush-after redirect is pending, wrong-path frontend instructions must not reach decode. In particular, a wrong-path `vset*` must not update `vconfig`, and the following correct-path vector instruction must see the pre-redirect vector configuration. Affected function: CtrlBlock handling of frontend `cfVec` inputs while a redirect is pending. Trigger condition: A flush-after redirect, such as a memory-violation redirect, is raised; then a wrong-path `vset*` arrives before the redirect fully takes effect; then a correct-path vector instruction is decoded.

import xiangshan.frontend.{BrType, Ftq}

class Ftq1931RegressionTest extends XSTester with Matchers {
  behavior of "Ftq PR1931 regression"

  it should "skip an empty redirected entry and commit the following taken entry" in {
    test(new Ftq()(config)).withAnnotations(Seq(
      VerilatorBackendAnnotation,
      VerilatorFlags(Seq("--exe", "/home/xiangshan/src/test/resources/ftqtable_stub.cpp"))
    )) { dut =>
      def zeroData(x: Data): Unit = x match {
        case r: Record => r.elements.values.foreach(zeroData)
        case v: Vec[_] => v.getElements.foreach(zeroData)
        case b: Bool => b.poke(false.B)
        case u: UInt => u.poke(0.U)
        case s: SInt => s.poke(0.S)
        case _ => throw new IllegalArgumentException("unsupported data")
      }

      val lastOffset = ((1 << dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqOffset.getWidth) - 1).U
      val lastIndex = lastOffset.litValue.toInt
      val entry0Pc = "h1000".U
      val entry1Pc = "h2000".U
      val entry1Target = "h4000".U

      def clearInputs(): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBpu.resp.valid.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.valid.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.valid.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits.foreach { c =>
          c.valid.poke(false.B)
          zeroData(c.bits)
        }
        dut.io.toIfu.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.toICache.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.toPrefetch.req.ready.poke(false.B)
        zeroData(dut.io.mmioCommitRead.mmioFtqPtr)
      }

      def enqueueEntry(ftqIdx: Int, pc: UInt, taken: Boolean, target: UInt): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBpu.resp.valid.poke(true.B)
        for (stage <- Seq(dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits.s1, dut.io.fromBpu.resp.bits.s3)) {
          stage.valid.poke(true.B)
          stage.pc.poke(pc)
          stage.ftq_idx.flag.poke(false.B)
          stage.ftq_idx.value.poke(ftqIdx.U)
          stage.full_pred.hit.poke(taken.B)
          if (taken) {
            stage.full_pred.slot_valids.last.poke(true.B)
            stage.full_pred.offsets.last.poke(lastOffset)
            stage.full_pred.targets.last.poke(target)
            stage.full_pred.is_jal.poke(true.B)
          }
        }
      }

      def redirectEntry(ftqIdx: Int): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(ftqIdx.U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.ftqOffset.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.level.poke(RedirectLevel.flushAfter)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.taken.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.target.poke("h3000".U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.redirect.bits.cfiUpdate.isMisPred.poke(true.B)
      }

      def writeBackTakenEntry1(): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(1.U)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pc(lastIndex).poke(entry1Pc)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).isRVC.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.pd(lastIndex).brType.poke(BrType.jal)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.instrRange(lastIndex).poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.cfiOffset.valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.cfiOffset.bits.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.target.poke(entry1Target)
        dut.io.fromIfu.pdWb.bits.jalTarget.poke(entry1Target)
      }

      def commitTakenEntry1(): Unit = {
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).valid.poke(true.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqIdx.flag.poke(false.B)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqIdx.value.poke(1.U)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.ftqOffset.poke(lastOffset)
        dut.io.fromBackend.rob_commits(0).bits.commitType.poke(0.U)
      }

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      enqueueEntry(0, entry0Pc, taken = false, target = 0.U)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      redirectEntry(0)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      enqueueEntry(1, entry1Pc, taken = true, target = entry1Target)
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      writeBackTakenEntry1()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      dut.clock.step()

      clearInputs()
      commitTakenEntry1()
      dut.clock.step()

      var sawUpdate = false
      for (_ <- 0 until 6) {
        clearInputs()
        sawUpdate ||= dut.io.toBpu.update.valid.peek().litToBoolean
        dut.clock.step()
      }

      sawUpdate shouldBe true
    }
  }
}
EOF

status=0
timeout 1200s mill -i XiangShan.test.testOnly "$TEST_CLASS" >"$RUN_LOG" 2>&1 || status=$?

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [[ "$status" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

cat "$RUN_LOG"
exit "$status"
problem_statement: The frontend FTQ (fetch target queue) tracks fetched instruction blocks and emits branch predictor (BPU) updates when a taken branch or jump entry commits. After redirect recovery, an older FTQ entry can end up with no surviving instructions, yet it still blocks the FTQ commit pointer. In that state, a younger FTQ entry behind it can write back and commit a taken branch or jump, but the expected branch predictor update is never emitted. The affected logic is the FTQ commit-state and commit-pointer handling during redirect recovery. The bug is triggered when a redirect empties an older FTQ entry and a later FTQ entry then commits a taken control-flow instruction. Expected behavior: an FTQ entry that becomes empty after redirect recovery must not block commit progress, so the following valid taken entry can commit normally and generate its branch predictor update.

This commit aims to fix dcache plru access logic

In the previous version, when a cacheline not in l1 is accessed, a replace way
is picked and used to update l1 plru (set the way as lru). However, if the same
missed cacheline is accessed multiple times before l1 refill, l1 will pick a new
replace way and use it to update plru for each time the missed cacheline is
accessed. It makes the plru totally a mess.

To fix that problem, extra condition check is added for a missed load plru
update. Now plru is updated on:

* load/store hit (touch hit way)
* load/store primary miss (touch replacement way)
* load/store secondary miss (touch replacement way)

+    when(victim_vec(set) =/= Fill(width, 1.U)) {
+      victim_vec(set) := victim_vec(set) + 1.U
+    }
+  }
+
+  def whether_sa(set:UInt) = victim_vec(set)(width-1)
+}
+
+trait WayConflictPredictParameters extends HasDCacheParameters {
+  val WCPSize = DCacheSets
+  val IdxBits = log2Up(WCPSize)
+  val CounterSize = 2
+  val PCOffBits = 2
+  def get_pc_idx(pc: UInt) = { pc(IdxBits+PCOffBits, PCOffBits)}
+  def get_addr_idx(addr: UInt) = { addr(IdxBits+DCacheSetOffset,DCacheSetOffset)}
+}
+
+abstract class WayConflictPredictorBundle(implicit P: Parameters) extends XSBundle with WayConflictPredictParameters
+abstract class WayConflictPredictorModule(implicit P: Parameters) extends XSModule with WayConflictPredictParameters
+
+class WayConflictPredIO (implicit p: Parameters) extends WayConflictPredictorBundle {
+  val en = Input(Bool())
+  val vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  val way_conflict = Output(Bool())
+}
+
+class WayConflictUpdIO (implicit p: Parameters) extends WayConflictPredictorBundle {
+  val en = Input(Bool())
+  val vaddr = Input(UInt(VAddrBits.W))
+  val dm_hit = Input(Bool())
+  val sa_hit = Input(Bool())
+}
+
+class WayConflictPredictor (nPorts: Int) (implicit p: Parameters) extends WayConflictPredictorModule{
+  val io = IO(new Bundle() {
+    val pred = Vec(nPorts, new WayConflictPredIO)
+    val update = Vec(nPorts, new WayConflictUpdIO)
+  })
+  val PredTable = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(WCPSize)(0.U(CounterSize.W))))
+
+  for (i <- 0 until nPorts){
+    io.pred(i).way_conflict := io.pred(i).en & PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.pred(i).vaddr))(CounterSize-1)
+    // saturation counter
+    when(io.update(i).en && io.update(i).sa_hit) {
+      when(PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) === Fill(CounterSize, 1.U)) {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+      }.otherwise {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) + 1.U
+      }
+    }.elsewhen(io.update(i).en && io.update(i).dm_hit) {
+      when(PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) === Fill(CounterSize, 0.U)) {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+      }.otherwise {
+        PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) - 1.U
+      }
+    }.otherwise {
+      PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr)) := PredTable(get_addr_idx(io.update(i).vaddr))
+    }
+  }
+
+}
